page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server is equipped with 945 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional memory subsystem capabilities. The server achieves a top-tier rating in the Passmark memory score, supported by strong large-block memory bandwidth results, reaching 304.72 GB/sec for read-only operations and 123.05 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 33.05 GB/sec. Other compute benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall within the average range. Large-model LLM inference shows limitations, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model performing in the lower tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16pds_v6 offers a high-density memory profile and fast local NVMe storage on an ARM architecture, which typically translates to lower resource overhead compared to traditional x86 architectures. This makes the server highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers that benefit from high memory bandwidth and fast local storage, while avoiding workloads requiring specialized vector or matrix extensions.
